Issued at 123 AM CDT Mon Sep 21 2026

As of 1am the large and wavy ridge continues to our north and 
beneath this, a persistent and slow moving upper level low is 
spinning over southern/southwestern SD and northern NE border. This 
is continuing to bring bands of rain showers to the region with the 
bulk of the moisture over southeastern to east central SD with more 
spotty precip over central SD as the bands tracks north and west per 
counterclockwise flow. Through the morning, this low will continue 
to track east and southeast along the border (and weaken) with the 
open wave over ~NE/IA border by 21Z. As this system moves out rain 
will diminish northwest to southeast (used a blend of 
NBM/Conshort/ECAM) with the last of the rain exiting east central SD 
this afternoon. QPF (or additional rain for some) ranges from around 
a quarter to potentially half of an inch over portions of south 
central to east central SD with QPF decreasing significantly, to a 
couple hundredths of an inch to nothing, the further north and 
northeast in the CWA due to the storm track as well as drier air 
from a large mid level to surface high that resides over Ontario. 
With the region on the western to southwestern side of this high, 
overall dry conditions are expected tonight. Dry weather continues 
Tuesday, however, weak shortwave energy (under the ongoing ridge) 
will be over the region which will bring back some clouds to the CWA 
and slight chances of pops over portions of south central SD in the 
afternoon. With help from an increasing LLJ (25-35kts), the chance 
of light rain spreads, as both EC/GEFS does highlight this. NBM 
indicate spotty coverage of pops of 20-45% across central SD, 
highest over far south central SD (mainly Lyman/Buffalo counties and 
southward Tuesday night/early Wednesday.

As the high drifts off towards the east/northeast, a negative tilted 
shortwave will track northeast (that developed over southern 
CA/Pacific) and move in over the western Dakotas/MT/WY Wednesday 
evening and tracking over ND/MN through Thursday morning. There is a 
bit of a difference between the models on exact track and intensity 
of this trough at this time. This will bring the return of moisture 
to the area with models at this point having the precip move in over 
north central SD Wednesday morning and becoming more widespread 
across the CWA by Wednesday night (NBM pops 50-80%) with rain ending 
west to east across the CWA by Thursday afternoon as the shortwave 
exits the region. Again, timing between models varies a bit on when 
the last of the rain exit with GEPS being the slowest. Probability 
of 24hr QPF>0.25", ending 12Z Thursday is 35-65% from north central 
through northeastern SD/western MN, highest over northern Corson 
into ND and along and east of the Coteau. With this -PNA 
pattern setting up for the end of the week, another shortwave 
moves in for Friday (per southwesterly flow). This feature 
interacting with southerly flow and pulling in moisture will 
result in additional rain chances Friday/Saturday. Low 
confidence in exact setup/track at this time and overall 
coverage of rain. As of now NBM pops ranges from 20-40% along 
and east of the Mo River and highest James Valley and eastward. 

Our windiest day of the week will be Tuesday afternoon (west of the 
Mo River of 20-30kts) as the high exits and increasing pressure 
gradient on the back side of it and east of a lee front. This 
increased gradient/development of a 30kts LLJ, the gusty winds will 
spread eastward across the CWA through Wednesday afternoon with NBM 
gusts between 20-35kts. Ongoing easterly flow at 850mb to surface 
(and lingering clouds) will keep temps cool again today withs highs 
in the upper 50s to the lower to mid 60s. Low level winds will be 
more southeasterly for Tuesday, but with the high still influencing 
the area, temps will only warm up a few degrees with highs overall 
in the 60s. South to southwest flow (and high moves out) will lead 
to temps warming back up to above normal with the warmer air 
spreading eastward across the CWA for the end of the week with 
highs in the upper 60s and 70s.
